key_insight: Thermodynamic and diffusion simulations link austenite formation during cooling to chromium nitride precipitation in duplex stainless steels and weld metal.
engineering_relevance: Controlling nitrogen content, ferrite grain size, and cooling history can help balance austenite recovery against unwanted nitride and intermetallic formation during welding.
method: Used computational thermodynamics and Thermo-Calc DICTRA diffusion modeling.
Studied nitrogen content, grain size, and cooling rate in LDX 2101, 2507, and 2509 weld filler.
Compared linear and non-linear cooling histories.
evidence_signal: Simulations agreed well with published experiments using critical austenite spacing for nitride precipitation and reproduced nitride-free zones adjacent to austenite.
watch_item: Cooling-history assumptions require care, and the abstract reports no quantitative error metrics for the experimental comparison.
paper_title: Thermodynamic modeling of chromium nitride precipitation in duplex stainless steels and weld metals
